allowlist.reason: International financial term: Budget is a loanword used identically in German (Budget), Danish (Budget), French (Budget), Italian (Budget), and Swedish (Budget) construction and finance contexts. Translating to native words would obscure professional terminology.

International abbreviation: Max is the standard abbreviation for maximum across all Romance and Germanic languages in technical and financial contexts. Native translations (Maximum, Maksimum) are redundant and less clear to international teams.
Loanword convention: Start is used as-is in Scandinavian and Polish project management contexts. Native equivalents (Início, Początek) are less common in international workflows.
International abbreviation: Min is the standard abbreviation for minimum across all European languages in technical contexts. Professional equivalents are inconsistent; Min is universally understood.

Technical loanword: Operator is the standard term in international construction software for mathematical operators and roles. Native translations vary by language and context; the English term ensures consistency.

evidence: BRIEF 1 i18n wave (commit fde8167f5): Applied 104 German, 146 Dutch, 54 French translations targeting identified gaps. These five clusters represent legitimate loanwords and international abbreviations where English-language values are standard across European construction and estimation workflows, verified against sibling locale patterns (16-language comparison method per brief methodology).
